history.gap: The five chart plates are rhythmically identical (card, caption row, one-line body, repeat) so the section reads as a list rather than a designed spread; the caption row itself (number · bold small caps · dotted leader · grey link) is a stock editorial pattern executed at 11px with no scale contrast to the plates above it. At the bar, plates would vary in scale and grid position (a full-bleed pair, then a narrow inset with a wide margin note), captions would carry a real secondary type size, and the mono annotations on mobile ("EQUAL HIGHS", "TRENDLINE LIQUIDITY", "FVG") would be re-laid rather than left colliding with candles and fib labels.
history.motion: Restrained fade-and-rise reveals with a clipped vertical wipe on the chart plates; competent, consistent, but generic and never surprising.
history.verdict: A is a disciplined, tightly kerned dark-editorial system whose only crime is safeness: every hairline, leader and mono label sits where it should, and the SVG chart tracings with gold annotations are genuinely distinctive material. B has the more cinematic ambition and a beautiful first photograph, but it fails the basic craft gates of contrast, label collision, dead space and copy proofing, so A takes it clearly without reaching shortlist.

history.gap: The chart annotations are where the editorial system falls apart at close range: in figure 03 "FVG" and "SELLSIDE LIQUIDITY" collide in the bottom-right corner, in 02 the Fibonacci levels (1.3414, 1.272, -0.272) are set at roughly 6px and the "SELLSIDE LIQUIDITY" label wraps against the frame edge, and the two abutting charts in 01 show a doubled seam where their borders meet. At the bar every label inside a chart is set at the same tracked small-cap size as the captions outside it, with leader lines rather than stacked text, and paired charts share a single hairline. On mobile those in-chart labels shrink to illegibility while the caption system stays perfect, which makes the mismatch obvious.
history.motion: Restrained staged fades with charts clip-revealing from the left and rotated section labels riding the rail; nothing spectacular but nothing misfires, and the pacing respects the reading rhythm.
history.verdict: B is a genuine editorial system, with numbered figures, dotted leaders, gold small caps against a serif measure, hairline rails, and charts that break the column with intent; its failures are micro-typographic inside the charts and fixable in an afternoon. A is a familiar dark-agency template whose one big idea (type over a small image) undercuts its own legibility, and whose mobile build has overlap bugs and dead space that no jury would forgive.
